firstMismatch.sourceBehavior: apply.c:use_royal_jelly -> timeout.c:kill_egg timer cancellation; later hatch timing changes
firstMismatch.details: The first downstream comparator divergence occurs at gethungry (C rn2(20)=1 versus JS rnd(1)=1) after the uncanceled JS egg timer changes later turns. The causal source gap is the omitted kill_egg cancellation, not gethungry itself. The recipe uses !safe_wait and a level change to prevent safe-wait occupation from obscuring the timer path.

summary: C cancels a timed egg’s HATCH_EGG timer through timeout.c:kill_egg. The JavaScript callers now share that implementation in the cursed-jelly, genocide-sweep, and hero-laid-egg polymorph branches.

source.branch: A timed EGG is made permanently unhatchable when cursed royal jelly is applied, when genocide finds an egg of a dead species, or when polymorph converts a hero-laid egg into a generic egg. C calls kill_egg(), whose sole state change is stopping that object’s HATCH_EGG timer.
callers: cmd.c:1678 dispatches the apply command to apply.c:doapply; doapply calls use_royal_jelly at apply.c:1800. The #rub command is registered at cmd.c:1836 and dorub calls use_royal_jelly at apply.c:4263. JS dispatch is cmd.js:3286-3293 to apply.js:doapply/dorub; apply.js:2241 and 4888 reach use_royal_jelly. The admitted v39 recipe exercises the #rub entry.

mon.c:kill_genocided_monsters calls kill_eggs for monster inventories and four object lists; active C callers include scroll/spell genocide (read.c:2749,2993), wizard level change (cmd.c:1048), and level arrival (do.c:1817). JS counterparts are read.js:2799,3024, cmd.js:2633, and do.js:3060.

zap.c:bhito invokes poly_obj for a floor object affected by polymorph; bhito is used by bhitpile and dozap. The z command dispatches to dozap at cmd.c:2005. JS wiring is cmd.js:3320 to zap.js:dozap, then zap.js:bhitpile/bhito to zap.js:poly_obj.
dependencies: timeout.c:stop_timer is already ported as js/timeout.js:stop_timer; C discards its return value.
